# SBC Thermal Analysis — is active cooling required?

**Subject:** `SBC3` NanoPi M5 (Rockchip RK3576, 4 GB) on the Phase-2 printed deck  
**Question:** `R4_SBC_TEMP` requires operation *"without active cooling"*, but the 
Phase-2 BOM carries a 30 mm fan. Is the fan actually needed?  
**Generated by** `analysis/sbc_thermal_analysis.py` — rerun to regenerate.

---

## Verdict

**The fan is needed — but not to fly.** The binding case is the aircraft sitting still 
at full inference load, not the aircraft in the air.

1. **In flight, passive cooling works.** Rotor inflow gives an estimated 
   **0.98–2.61 m/s** over the deck; a full-board sink needs 
   **0.60 m/s** shaded or **0.92 m/s** in direct sun. Junction lands at 
   **74 °C** at the conservative low end 
   (72 °C with a light-finish sink) against an 85 °C trip.
2. **On the ground at full load, passive fails outright** — **116 °C** on a 
   35 °C pad in sun, and §7 shows no plausible model error or airflow assumption rescues it. 
   That is exactly the condition of bench development, model loading, pre-flight and the 
   `VB-02` / `VB-03` acceptance tests.
3. **The heatsink matters more than the fan.** The SoC-sized 40×40 sink fails even at the 
   *high* propwash estimate (**78 °C**); the full-board sink passes at the low 
   one. A light finish instead of black anodising is worth ~13 °C on the pad, for free.

### Recommended disposition

| # | Action | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Keep the 30 mm fan**, but reclassify it as *ground/bench thermal support* — not a flight-critical item | Ground full-load operation needs it; flight does not. Its failure in flight is then benign by design, which is what the original 'no active cooling' intent was protecting |
| 2 | **Specify a full-board heatsink (~80×55 mm) with a light or clear finish** — not the SoC-sized sink, not black anodised | Single highest-value change, and it is free. The small sink fails every case |
| 3 | **Restate `R4_SBC_TEMP`** | *'Without active cooling'* is not achievable at 10 W sustained, and the requirement never defines the environmental range it refers to |
| 4 | **Gate sustained full-load inference to in-flight phases** | Idle (4 W) is comfortable passively; the mission app already starts inference at takeoff |

Proposed requirement text:

> The SBC shall operate without thermal throttling at sustained maximum inference load 
> (10 W board power) over an ambient range of 0–40 °C, using passive cooling plus 
> rotor-induced airflow, in all flight phases. Forced-air cooling is permitted for ground 
> operation and shall not be flight-critical: loss of the cooling fan shall not prevent 
> compliance in any flight phase.

This keeps the original intent — *never depend on a fan to stay airborne* — while matching 
what the physics allows. It is testable, and `VB-03` closes it.

---

## 1. Limits and heat load

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|---|--:|---|
| SoC throttle trip (DVFS passive) | 85 °C | Rockchip thermal-zone config |
| Required design margin below trip | 10 °C | this analysis |
| Board max ambient (spec) | 70 °C | FriendlyElec NanoPi M5 |
| Board power, full inference | 10.0 W | `R4_SBC_PWR` cap / `SBC3.power` |
| Board power, idle | 4.0 W | `SBC3.idlePower` |
| Fraction dissipated in the SoC | 70% | assumed; rest is DDR/PMIC/PHY on the PCB |
| Conduction path R_jc + R_tim | 2.5 K/W | FCBGA + thermal pad |

## 2. In-flight airflow (actuator-disk theory)

Reference config C000009 — AF3a Chimera9 ECO, AUW **1750 g**, 9" props, 
hover throttle 14.9 %. Same momentum theory the endurance sweep uses:

- Thrust per rotor: **4.29 N**
- Induced velocity at the disk: **v_i = 6.53 m/s**
- Fully-contracted wake: 13.07 m/s

The 90 × 62 mm board sits centred on the top deck, spanning ~55 mm from centre at its 
corners. The rotor disks begin ~88 mm out (405 mm wheelbase, 114 mm prop radius), so the 
SBC sits **inboard of the disks, in the inflow field feeding them** — not in the wake. 
Taking 15%–40% of v_i at the hub gives 
**0.98–2.61 m/s** over the sink. The analysis designs to the 
bottom of that band (0.98 m/s) and reports sensitivity below.

> The board is the topmost item on the airframe (raised tier above the top-mounted 
> battery), which maximises its exposure to that inflow — and to the sun.

## 3. What can physically mount (measured from the layout drawing)

The M5 is not a flat surface, and this constrains the sink harder than the thermals do. 
Measured off the official LPDDR4X layout at 5.0 px/mm, from the PCB top edge:

| Band (from top edge) | Occupant | Height |
|---|---|---|
| 0 – 18 mm | 2× RJ45, 2× USB-A, HDMI | **~14–20 mm — hard keep-out** |
| 21 – 28 mm | RTL8211F Ethernet PHYs | low-profile QFN |
| 32 – 49 mm | **RK3576 SoC (~16×16 mm)** | ~1.5 mm — the only contact that matters |
| 55 – 62 mm | 30-pin GPIO header | ~8.5 mm |

Across the board from the left edge: buttons to ~5 mm, LPDDR4X 11–23 mm, SoC 29–46 mm, 
M.2 E-Key socket from ~53 mm, microSD from ~76 mm.

**Usable flush-mount window: ~47 × 35 mm** — it clears the connector row, stops 
short of the M.2 E-Key, and covers both the SoC and the LPDDR4X.

> **A large flat block cannot work at any thickness.** Laid on the board it rests on the 
> 14–20 mm connector row, leaving a ~15 mm air gap over the SoC — no thermal contact. The 
> board's mounting holes (~83 × 42 mm spacing) match no COTS heatsink pattern either, so 
> attachment is by thermal adhesive pad onto the SoC package.

This window is only ~37 % of the 80 × 55 mm footprint assumed in an earlier revision of this 
analysis. Lost base area has to be recovered through **fin height**, not footprint.

### Sinks modelled

| Sink | Wetted area | Footprint | Fin gap | Est. mass |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 40x40x10 mm (SoC-sized kit part) | 115 cm² | 16 cm² | 2.5 mm | ~26 g |
| 47x35x25 mm (fits M5 clear area) | 246 cm² | 16 cm² | 3.0 mm | ~48 g |

Fin-height trade within the fixed 47 × 35 mm window (full load, 35 °C, in sun):

| Fin height | Wetted area | Est. mass | Flight (low propwash) | Flight, light finish | Pad, still air |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 15 mm | 152 cm² | ~34 g | 86 °C ❌ | 82 °C ⚠️ | 141 °C ❌ |
| 20 mm | 199 cm² | ~41 g | 79 °C ⚠️ | 76 °C ⚠️ | 126 °C ❌ |
| 25 mm | 246 cm² | ~48 g | 74 °C ✅ | 72 °C ✅ | 116 °C ❌ |
| 30 mm | 293 cm² | ~54 g | 71 °C ✅ | 69 °C ✅ | 109 °C ❌ |
| 35 mm | 340 cm² | ~61 g | 69 °C ✅ | 67 °C ✅ | 103 °C ❌ |

**25 mm of fin is the floor** for a passing flight case; 30 mm buys comfortable margin. 
Below 20 mm the flight case fails even before considering model error. No fin height 
rescues still-air ground operation.

## 5. How much airflow is actually needed?

Full inference load, 35 °C ambient, in sun — sweeping airflow over the sink:

| Airflow | 40x40x10 mm (SoC-sized kit part) | 47x35x25 mm (fits M5 clear area) |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 m/s | 155 °C ❌ | 116 °C ❌ |
| 0.25 m/s | 127 °C ❌ | 94 °C ❌ |
| 0.50 m/s | 108 °C ❌ | 82 °C ⚠️ |
| 0.75 m/s | 98 °C ❌ | 77 °C ⚠️ |
| 1.00 m/s | 93 °C ❌ | 74 °C ✅ |
| 1.50 m/s | 86 °C ❌ | 70 °C ✅ |
| 2.00 m/s | 82 °C ⚠️ | 68 °C ✅ |
| 3.00 m/s | 76 °C ⚠️ | 65 °C ✅ |
| 5.00 m/s | 71 °C ✅ | 63 °C ✅ |

- **40x40x10 mm (SoC-sized kit part)** — minimum airflow to pass: **3.43 m/s** in sun, **2.28 m/s** shaded.
- **47x35x25 mm (fits M5 clear area)** — minimum airflow to pass: **0.92 m/s** in sun, **0.60 m/s** shaded.

Available in flight at the hub: **0.98–2.61 m/s**.

## 6. Heatsink finish (daytime mission, board on top)

Solar gain is not a rounding error here — on the larger sink it rivals the SoC's own 
dissipation. Finish is a free lever:

| Finish | Absorptivity | Q_solar | T_j — pad, still, full load, 35 °C |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Black anodised | 0.95 | 1.6 W | 116 °C |
| Bare / clear / light | 0.30 | 0.5 W | 110 °C |

## 7. Sensitivity — where the conclusion actually comes from

The in-flight verdict is close enough to the line that it is worth showing exactly which 
assumptions carry it. Both are swept on the full-board sink at full load, 35 °C, in sun.

**(a) Hub inflow fraction** — the least-supported number in the model:

| Fraction of v_i | Airflow | T_j | Verdict |
|--:|--:|--:|:--:|
| 10% | 0.65 m/s | 79 °C | ⚠️ |
| 15% | 0.98 m/s | 74 °C | ✅ |
| 20% | 1.31 m/s | 72 °C | ✅ |
| 25% | 1.63 m/s | 70 °C | ✅ |
| 30% | 1.96 m/s | 68 °C | ✅ |
| 40% | 2.61 m/s | 66 °C | ✅ |
| 50% | 3.27 m/s | 65 °C | ✅ |

**(b) Model conservatism** — the still-air fin derate and the correlations together carry 
roughly ±25 %. Re-running the still-air pad case with R_sa scaled:

| R_sa scaling | T_j — pad, still, full load, 35 °C + sun | Verdict |
|--:|--:|:--:|
| 0.75× (optimistic) | 100 °C | ❌ |
| 1.00× (nominal) | 116 °C | ❌ |
| 1.25× (pessimistic) | 132 °C | ❌ |

**(c) Actual heat load** — 10 W is the `R4_SBC_PWR` *cap*, not a measurement. FriendlyElec 
publishes no power figure for the M5; Rockchip quotes RK3576 TDP "<15 W" (SoC only), and 
third-party comparisons put it 20–40 % below the RK3588's ~12 W, i.e. **~7–10 W**. Sweeping 
the credible band (full-board sink, 35 °C, in sun):

| Board power | Board heat | Pad, still air | Flight, low propwash |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 W | 4.2 W | 86 °C ❌ | 57 °C ✅ |
| 6 W | 5.2 W | 92 °C ❌ | 60 °C ✅ |
| 7 W | 6.2 W | 98 °C ❌ | 64 °C ✅ |
| 8 W | 7.2 W | 104 °C ❌ | 67 °C ✅ |
| 9 W | 8.2 W | 110 °C ❌ | 71 °C ✅ |
| 10 W | 9.2 W | 116 °C ❌ | 74 °C ✅ |

Even at the bottom of the credible band the still-air pad case does not clear the design 
margin. The flight case, by contrast, is comfortable across the whole band — so the 
conclusion is **not** an artifact of using the requirement cap as the heat load.

**(d) Why measuring input power is necessary but not sufficient.** For an SBC essentially 
100 % of electrical input becomes heat (no mechanical work; radiated RF/optical is 
negligible), less what is exported through the ports — here the T13 camera draws 
~0.8 W over USB. So a wall-plug measurement bounds the **total** heat load 
directly and exactly. What it cannot resolve is the **split** between the SoC package (which 
the heatsink sees, assumed 70% here) and the DDR / PMIC / PHY / USB devices, which 
reject into the PCB. That split is the difference between a comfortable pass and a fail:

| SoC share of board heat | T_j — flight, low propwash, 35 °C + sun | T_j — pad, still air |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 55% | 67 °C | 103 °C |
| 70% | 74 °C | 116 °C |
| 85% | 82 °C | 129 °C |
| 100% | 89 °C | 141 °C |

**The way out is not a better model — it is the on-die sensor.** The RK3576 exposes junction 
temperature at `/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp`. Logging input power *and* SoC 
temperature together, under the real workload on the as-built deck, measures the heat load 
and the assembly's actual thermal resistance simultaneously and retires every assumption 
in this document. **`VB-02` (power) and `VB-03` (thermal) should be run as one test.**

Read together: **no plausible combination rescues still-air operation at full load**, and 
the in-flight case flips on whether the hub sees more or less than ~20 % of v_i — which 
nobody has measured.

## 8. Assumptions and limits

- No published thermal test data exists for the NanoPi M5; this is a first-principles 
  bound. **VB-03 (bench thermal soak) is the closing evidence**, not this document.
- Laminar flat-plate and horizontal-plate correlations; real finned-sink performance 
  typically lands within ±25 % of this.
- The hub inflow fraction is an engineering estimate, not CFD or measurement. It is the 
  single most load-bearing assumption — hence designing to the low end.
- Fin area derated to 60% in still air and 90% in forced flow.
- Steady state only. Thermal mass buys a few minutes of transient headroom on the pad, 
  which is exactly the phase where the still-air cases are marginal.
- Board ambient spec is 70 °C; nothing here approaches that limit — the 
  binding constraint is the SoC junction, not the board rating.
